newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch supermarkets' turnover up 3.6 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dutch supermarkets' turnover up 3.6 pct in 1996.

text.p: Dutch supermarket turnover rose 3.6 percent to 41.7 billion guilders in 1996, the Central Bureau for Food Retailing (CBL) said on Tuesday.
Strong competition had broadly kept consumer prices from rising. Corrected for inflation, they even fell, it said.

The CBL said extended store opening hours had generated an increase of three percent in turnover in 1996 for those shops taking advantage of extended opening hours past 6 p.m., introduced in June 1996.
The introduction of the euro is expected to cost Dutch supermarkets 700 million guilders, about 1.5 percent of turnover.

According to a poll carried out on behalf of the CBL, 83 percent of Dutch consumers feel the state should pay for these costs, 11 percent of consumers think banks should pay, while six percent feel consumers or shopkeepers should pay the bill.
The CBL groups all 7,000 supermarkets in the Netherlands.
